---
title: "How do I estimate a confidence interval for a population mean?"
---

## Question

How do I estimate a confidence interval for a population mean?

## Decide which method fits

Select the relevant sample, choose and disclose the confidence level; calculate a t interval and explain its repeated-sampling interpretation.

## Worked example: PlantGrowth

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("PlantGrowth")
control <- subset(d, group=="ctrl")
fit <- ru_apply("mean_confidence_interval", control,
                x="weight", confidence=.95)
stopifnot(length(fit$conf.int)==2L)
```

The interval concerns the mean weight of observations in the selected control group, under sampling and model assumptions. 95% is the long-run coverage of the procedure, not a probability that a fixed mean moves between endpoints.

## Apply to another dataset

```r
ru_apply("mean_confidence_interval", your_data, x="numeric_column", confidence=.95)
```

If the question concerns a proportion rather than a numeric mean, use proportion_interval. If two groups are contrasted, check the design before selecting an appropriate two-sample method.

Review assumptions and available input conditions with `ru_plan("mean_confidence_interval")`. A valid computation does not itself verify the underlying study design.
